Moving between rentals: fund the new deposit before the old one comes back

Follow four interactive charts through a six-month move budget, separating upfront cash, extra overlap rent, refund timing and the buffer you want to preserve.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore a hypothetical six-month rental move

Original hypothetical six-month cash-timing model in nominal CAD. Regular rent and living costs are already covered outside this ledger; the monthly amount is the surplus available afterward. The new deposit is paid at the start of month 1; extra overlap rent and moving/setup costs at the start of month 2. Monthly surplus and any assumed old-deposit refund arrive at month-end. Negative positions identify an unfunded need using the entered resources, not an actual overdraft or an assumed loan. The solved additional initial cash is shown separately and is not silently added to the charts. The refund amount and month are independent assumptions, not a legal entitlement or deadline. Month 7 means no refund within these six months. The new deposit is not returned within the window. No interest, borrowing, tax, deposit eligibility or dispute outcome is calculated. The selected buffer is a personal scenario input, not a recommended minimum.

The central idea

A refundable deposit can still create a cash shortage. Match payments and expected receipts to dates, then fund the lowest point rather than relying on the final total.

01

A move has both a cost budget and a cash calendar

A move can look affordable when you subtract an expected deposit refund from the total bill. The payment calendar may tell a different story. Your next landlord may need a deposit while your previous landlord still holds the old one. Movers and extra rent may also be payable before the next amount you can save from income.

The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada’s renting guide includes account setup charges, moving services and supplies among the costs to consider. Those categories help build a complete budget. This article adds a second step: assign the cash movements to dates.

All amounts in the tool are hypothetical CAD inputs. They are not estimates of local rent, typical moving charges or legally permitted deposits. The six-month window begins when the new deposit is paid; it is not a legal notice or refund period.

02

Keep the regular household budget outside the move ledger

The default scenario starts with CAD 2,500 already available for the move. It adds CAD 400 at each month-end. That monthly amount is what remains after regular rent, groceries, utilities, debt payments and other continuing commitments. It is not gross salary or the whole bank deposit from a paycheque.

Extra overlap rent is the additional rent caused by carrying both places beyond the regular rent already allowed for in your household budget. Entering both full rental payments here after also deducting regular rent elsewhere would count part of the cost twice. If the new ongoing rent is higher, update your regular budget before choosing the monthly surplus.

The assumed old-deposit refund is also separate from the opening cash. Money still held by someone else is not part of the amount available today. If it has already arrived and is included in your opening cash, set the future refund input to zero.

03

Find the low point before counting later receipts

The model pays a CAD 1,200 new deposit at the start of month 1. The move pool falls from CAD 2,500 to CAD 1,300, then the month-end surplus raises it to CAD 1,700. At the start of month 2, CAD 2,000 of extra rent and CAD 1,500 of moving/setup costs create a funding position of minus CAD 1,800.

That negative number is an unmet need using the selected resources. The model has not arranged a loan or assumed a bank will honour an overdraft. A CAD 1,000 refund at the end of month 3 improves the later arithmetic but cannot pay a bill due at the start of month 2.

The line chart shows both the position after bills and the position after receipts. Its default low point is minus CAD 1,800, even though the six-month endpoint is positive CAD 1,200. Looking only at the final balance would miss the earlier financing problem.

04

Calculate the initial amount needed to preserve your selected buffer

Choose the cash amount you want to keep available throughout the move. The default is CAD 500 as an illustration, not a prescribed reserve. The required additional initial cash equals the greater of zero and the selected buffer minus the lowest before-receipt funding position.

At the defaults, CAD 500 minus negative CAD 1,800 is CAD 2,300. Adding that amount before month 1 would shift every point upward by CAD 2,300 and leave CAD 500 at the modeled low point. The chart continues to show the entered resources so that the original shortfall remains visible; it does not quietly assume you have found the extra money.

Possible changes include saving more before committing, reducing quoted moving costs or changing the assumed overlap. Test changes separately to see which payment date they affect. If borrowing is considered, its availability, fees and repayments need a separate household cash plan.

05

Stress the refund without treating a scenario as a legal deadline

Move the refund from month 3 to month 5, then choose 7 to put it outside the six-month window. Try a smaller refund as a separate test. These assumptions show how much the plan depends on a receipt whose timing or amount still needs confirmation. A refund outside the chart is not assumed to be permanently lost.

Deposit rules and processes depend on the jurisdiction and tenancy. As one local example, British Columbia’s deposit guidance describes condition inspections, a written forwarding address and procedures for returning or retaining deposits. Check the applicable process and actual records before treating a refund as available cash. This calculator determines no entitlement, lawful deposit cap or statutory deadline.

The sensitivity matrix counts months when the position before receipts is below your chosen buffer. It does not measure the size of the shortage: two scenarios can have the same count and very different dollar gaps. Read it alongside the low-point metric and the payment chart.

06

Use the endpoint as a reconciliation after checking the dates

The waterfall adds opening cash, six monthly transfers and the refund actually scheduled within the window. It subtracts the new deposit, extra rent and moving/setup costs. At the defaults, CAD 2,500 + CAD 2,400 + CAD 1,000 − CAD 1,200 − CAD 2,000 − CAD 1,500 equals CAD 1,200.

The new deposit remains tied up throughout these six months. The tool does not assume that it returns on a convenient date, earns interest or can be substituted for a rent payment. Its eventual treatment belongs in the applicable agreement and local rules.

Keep a simple dated record of quotations, deposit payments, receipts and expected refunds. Update the plan as amounts become confirmed, while preserving enough cash for payments that arrive first. The useful result is a move schedule you can fund at each step.
